display: Da Nang / Hoi An / Lang Co
tagline: Central Vietnam's resort corridor — a UNESCO old town, a beach city and a lagoon, strung along one coast yet stitched together only by congested roads.
summary: The Da Nang–Hoi An–Lang Co corridor is one of Asia's densest luxury-resort coastlines — InterContinental Sun Peninsula, Four Seasons Nam Hai and a wall of beach resorts — anchored by a fast-growing airport city and the UNESCO town of Hoi An. Da Nang drew ~12.8 million visitors in the first eight months of 2025 (5M international). Yet every transfer between these waterfront destinations runs on coastal roads and the Cua Dai/Cham Island day-boat fleet. The coast itself is the natural highway — and it's barely used.

use_cases.title: Da Nang ↔ Hoi An coastal connector
use_cases.body: A clean foiling link from Da Nang's beach/riverfront to Hoi An (Cua Dai) bypasses congested coastal roads — a fast, smooth, scenic transfer between the beach city and the UNESCO town.

use_cases.title: Cham Islands clean day-trips
use_cases.body: Foiling to Cu Lao Cham (~24 nm from Da Nang, ~9 nm from Cua Dai) replaces a rough diesel speedboat crossing into a marine biosphere reserve with a faster, quieter, zero-emission ride better suited to a protected area.

use_cases.title: Resort-to-resort 'Navier Experience'
use_cases.body: Direct waterfront transfers between Son Tra (InterContinental Sun Peninsula), the My Khe beach resorts, Nam Hai and the Lang Co lagoon — a refined arrival and inter-resort link for high-spend guests.

journeys.from: Da Nang (My Khe / Han River waterfront)
journeys.today: 30–45 min by road that balloons with peak-season traffic; the scenic coast sits right there, unused.
journeys.with_navier: A direct ~16 nm foiling hop down the coast — smooth, fast, scenic and congestion-free between beach city and UNESCO town.

journeys.today: Diesel speedboat (~50 min) or slow ferry (~2.5h) into a marine biosphere reserve — noisy, exhaust-heavy and weather-sensitive.
journeys.with_navier: A quiet, near-wake-free foiling crossing well suited to a protected reserve, arriving fresh for diving and beach time.

journeys.today: Road over/through the Hai Van pass and tunnel — scenic but slow and indirect for a coastal destination.
journeys.with_navier: A direct coastal foiling leg (~16 nm) around the Son Tra peninsula; Quanta-LR extends the same clean corridor up to Chan May / Hue and south to Quang Nam.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Perfect for the corridor: Da Nang↔Hoi An (~16 nm), Da Nang↔Cham Islands (~24 nm), Cua Dai↔Cham (~9 nm) and Da Nang↔Lang Co (~16 nm) all sit well within the 70 nm all-electric envelope, with zero-emission appeal for the Cu Lao Cham biosphere reserve.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Stitches the wider central-coast network — Da Nang↔Chan May/Hue to the north and Da Nang↔Quang Ngai/Quy Nhon↔Nha Trang to the south — into longer hybrid line-haul legs beyond Pioneer II range, with no charging-infrastructure dependency along an under-equipped coast.

competitive_landscape: Inter-destination movement today is dominated by road transfer (taxis, shuttles, private cars) along an increasingly congested coastal corridor, plus a diesel speedboat/ferry fleet on the Cua Dai–Cham Islands run. There is no scheduled fast-water connector between Da Nang, Hoi An and Lang Co and no premium on-demand or zero-emission option — the coast is the obvious highway and it is essentially unused, which is the opportunity.
seasonality: The dry, calm season (Feb–Aug) is ideal for coastal foiling; the rainy season and NE monsoon (Sep–Dec) bring swell, storms and the period when the open Da Nang–Cham crossing gets rough and day-boats cancel. Foiling's stability, higher cruise speed and better sea-state handling keep the sheltered Da Nang↔Hoi An and Lang Co legs reliable and make the exposed Cham crossing far more comfortable on marginal days.
regulatory_note: Operations span Da Nang city and Quang Nam province authorities, with Cu Lao Cham designated a UNESCO Marine Biosphere Reserve — where a low-wake, zero-emission fleet aligns with conservation rules. Central Vietnam's tourism master-planning and the national net-zero-2050 commitment make a clean coastal-mobility network a policy tailwind.
